title: SDK Environment & Handshake Experiments — hosted API sketch
summary: Exploratory PRD sketch proposing a compact client handshake and progressive structured-output model for the Hosted API. Focused on incremental SDK ergonomics, deterministic tool-call lifecycle, and diagnostic-first streaming semantics.
content:
Context:
We keep iterating on how the Hosted API surfaces streaming and tool-calls to client libraries. The goal of this note is to propose an SDK-friendly "session environment" and handshake that: 1) reduces integration friction for typical web/mobile backends, 2) makes incremental structured output reliable for validators/consumers, and 3) preserves our latency/cost controls (batching, fallback). This is intentionally experimental: concrete API shape below is a set of trade experiments we want to play with in the next sprint.

Objectives:
- Provide a compact client-side session object (Sdkenv) that encodes capability/adaptive preferences and exposes lightweight lifecycle hooks.
- Standardize a handshake token exchange that sets streaming framing, schema expectations, and tool-call contract (verifiable at server side).
- Enable partial structured output that can be validated incrementally by SDKs with minimal parsing overhead.
- Offer ergonomic tool-call primitives (promise-like and callback) that are tolerant to partial frames, retries, and out-of-order tool resolution.
- Add a small set of observability breadcrumbs carried on the stream for debugging and telemetry without inflating user-visible tokens.

Key concepts (unique / experimental):
1) Sdkenv (compact session env):
   - small JSON (<= 1KB after base64) that describes client capabilities: prefer_low_latency, allow_partial_schemas, max_stream_chunks, tool_policy (sync|async|defer), debug_level.
   - server can use Sdkenv to pick a serving profile (fast-path, batch-friendly, cached).
   - Sdkenv is opaque to the app; SDKs construct with typed helpers.

2) Handshake v2 (lightweight capability negotiation):
   - client sends INIT frame with Sdkenv + schema id hash + optional prompt-prefetch hints. Server responds with ACCEPT frame containing: chosen_profile, clock_skew_ms, resume_token, and a list of tool_descriptors (id, version, capabilities).
   - resume_token is low-entropy (not secrets) used to map to server session for resumable streams.

3) Event watermarking + chunk envelopes:
   - stream emits CHUNK frames with envelope: {seq, watermark, payload_type, schema_tags, breadcrumbs}. 
   - watermark is an increasing logical timestamp used by SDKs to decide when it's safe to run validators or call downstream handlers.
   - schema_tags indicate which portion of structured schema the chunk attempts to satisfy (e.g., header, items/0, items/1, footer).

4) Progressive schema checking:
   - SDK exposes onPartial(schemaPath, partialValue) callback that automatically validates partial frames against lightweight subset rules.
   - Validation runs only on stable watermark thresholds to avoid flapping.

5) Tool-call lifecycle primitives:
   - Two ergonomic surfaces: callToolBlocking(toolId, args) -> Promise<Result> and callToolCallable(toolId, args, {onResolved}) -> Token.
   - Blocking is best-effort: server will try to resolve in the same stream; if it cannot (due to latency), it returns a tool_pending edge and the SDK receives a follow-up TOOL_RESOLVE frame with resolution or failure.
   - Token model allows apps to render a placeholder while waiting. Token carries a small id + tracing breadcrumb used for observability.

6) Backpressure & budget tokens:
   - To avoid uncontrolled client prefetching, server issues a budget_credit count in ACCEPT. Each CALL_TOOL consumes credit; SDKs must expose a simple flow-control hook so app devs can query remaining_credits.

7) Diagnostic breadcrumbs (low-cost):
   - Each CHUNK/frame can carry 0–3 breadcrumb keypairs (short codes, e.g., "rts": "p1", "dec": "q3"). Breadcrumbs are designed to be machine-readable and map to a server-side explanation for why certain fallbacks happened (e.g., model_fallback, quantized_path, cached_prefix_hit). SDKs include helpers to surface these as hints in logs or telemetry.

Developer ergonomics proposals (SDK):
- Tiny session object: Sdkenv.make({allowPartial:true, preferLowLatency:true}) returns a typed object that serializes for the INIT frame.
- StreamReader abstraction: async iterator but with added helpers: .onPartial(path, fn), .onToolToken(tokenId, onResolved), .pause()/resume() (maps to budget-credit consumption).
- Auto-validate toggle: sdkenv.validatePartial = "optimistic" | "strict". 'optimistic' runs subset checks and surfaces warnings instead of throwing.
- Offline replay helper: capture resume_token + last_seq to replay and continue in an offline worker. Useful for mobile clients that lost connectivity.

Operational constraints & SLO tradeoffs:
- Handshake adds ~1 roundtrip (INIT/ACCEPT) but enables more deterministic routing and less per-chunk negotiation. Acceptable when session length > 4k tokens.
- Progressive validation increases CPU on edge clients; set default to 'optimistic' to avoid noise.
- Budget-credit enforces cost predictability; default = 3 tool-calls per session for free-tier, configurable on Dedicated.

Security & compliance notes:
- Sdkenv must not contain secrets. Resume_token is low-entropy and must be authenticated server-side if used to access private state.
- Tool descriptors may advertise input data retention policies; SDK surfaces these at call-time so host apps can warn/consent.

Example flow (compact):
  Client -> INIT {sdkenv, schema_hash}
  Server -> ACCEPT {profile:fastpath, credits:3, resume_token:R-123, tools:[{id:search,v:2}]}
  Client -> STREAM: CHUNK(seq:1, watermark:10, payload_type:text, schema_tags:[header])
  Server -> STREAM: CHUNK(seq:2, watermark:12, payload_type:tool_call, payload:{tool_id:search,args:{q:"X"}}, breadcrumbs:["rts:p1"])
  Server -> TOOL_RESOLVE(token:T-42, result:{items:[...]})
  Server -> CHUNK(seq:3, watermark:20, payload_type:structured, schema_tags:[items/0])

Open questions / experiments to run:
- How often do client apps enable strict partial validation? (survey + dogfood)
- Accept frame payload size tradeoff — include full tool_descriptors vs. a reference id. Cost/latency impact for mobile edge connections.
- Budget-credit UX: should the SDK expose a soft token bucket or explicit per-call rejection?
- Resume semantics across model rollouts: if resume_token maps to an older model snapshot, do we allow deterministic replay or force resume->new session migration?

Acceptance criteria for spike (2 sprints):
- Prototype JS + Python SDK supporting Sdkenv, INIT/ACCEPT handshake, CHUNK envelopes, and a demo of callToolBlocking and Token-based tool resolution.
- Load test demonstrating <5% added tail latency for handshake-enabled sessions vs baseline for 90th percentile when session > 4k tokens.
- A small replayable example app (notes app with search tool) that uses resume_token to reconnect and resume partial structured output processing.

Next steps / owners:
- Prototype SDK surface: Arjun P. (JS) + Evelyn R. (Python) — week 1 spike to validate API ergonomics.
- Server-side routing hook: Serving/runtime team — Diego M. to design how Sdkenv maps to profile selection.
- Observability mapping: SRE/console — add breadcrumbs->reason code mapping in Console.

Notes to reviewers (rough):
- This intentionally mixes protocol ideas and SDK ergonomics; feedback requested especially on the token/budget model and resume semantics.
- We should avoid introducing heavyweight per-frame cryptography; rely on existing TLS + auth for sensitive operations.
- If approved, this becomes a mid-level experiment (non-breaking) that we can gate behind feature flags for Hosted.

Appendix: quick SDK snippet (JS-style pseudo):
  const env = Sdkenv.make({allowPartial:true, preferLowLatency:true});
  const s = await Redwood.hosted.stream({sdkenv:env, schemaHash: 'sha1:abc'});
  for await (const frame of s) {
    if (frame.type === 'chunk' && frame.schema_tags.includes('items/0')) {
      appRenderer.add(frame.payload);
    }
    if (frame.type === 'tool_resolve') {
      widgets.resolve(frame.token, frame.result);
    }
  }

Unresolved / TODO:
- Decide canonical field names for CHUNK envelope (seq vs offset, watermark naming).
- Define small-binary encoding vs JSON for CHUNK payloads (impact on mobile).
- Run cost model for credits on Hosted free-tier vs Dedicated.

End of sketch.

(If you want, I can take the prototype acceptance criteria and turn them into a short Linear backlog with tasks.)
